From 54f9d645a5453d0bfece0c465d34aaf072ea99fa Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jun Seo <jun.seo.93@proton.me>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 10:08:20 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] ALSA: usb-audio: Use correct version for UAC3 header
 validation

The entry of the validators table for UAC3 AC header descriptor is
defined with the wrong protocol version UAC_VERSION_2, while it should
have been UAC_VERSION_3.  This results in the validator never matching
for actual UAC3 devices (protocol == UAC_VERSION_3), causing their
header descriptors to bypass validation entirely.  A malicious USB
device presenting a truncated UAC3 header could exploit this to cause
out-of-bounds reads when the driver later accesses unvalidated
descriptor fields.

The bug was introduced in the same commit as the recently fixed UAC3
feature unit sub-type typo, and appears to be from the same copy-paste
error when the UAC3 section was created from the UAC2 section.

Fixes: 57f8770620e9 ("ALSA: usb-audio: More validations of descriptor units")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Jun Seo <jun.seo.93@proton.me>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260226010820.36529-1-jun.seo.93@proton.me
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>

diff --git a/sound/usb/validate.c b/sound/usb/validate.c
index 4bb4893f6e74..f62b7cc041dc 100644
--- a/sound/usb/validate.c
+++ b/sound/usb/validate.c
@@ -281,7 +281,7 @@ static const struct usb_desc_validator audio_validators[] = {
 	/* UAC_VERSION_2, UAC2_SAMPLE_RATE_CONVERTER: not implemented yet */
 
 	/* UAC3 */
-	FIXED(UAC_VERSION_2, UAC_HEADER, struct uac3_ac_header_descriptor),
+	FIXED(UAC_VERSION_3, UAC_HEADER, struct uac3_ac_header_descriptor),
 	FIXED(UAC_VERSION_3, UAC_INPUT_TERMINAL,
 	      struct uac3_input_terminal_descriptor),
 	FIXED(UAC_VERSION_3, UAC_OUTPUT_TERMINAL,
-- 
2.34.1

The patch corrects a copy-paste error in the USB audio descriptor validation table where the UAC3 AC header descriptor validator was incorrectly assigned protocol version `UAC_VERSION_2` instead of the correct `UAC_VERSION_3`.

**Modifications:**

- **`sound/usb/validate.c`**:  
  Changed the protocol version in the `FIXED` validator entry for `UAC_HEADER` from `UAC_VERSION_2` to `UAC_VERSION_3`. This ensures that the validator is matched for actual UAC3 devices (protocol == `UAC_VERSION_3`), enabling proper validation of the UAC3 AC header descriptor and preventing out-of-bounds reads from malformed descriptors.

**Relationship:**  
The single-line change aligns the validator entry with the intended UAC3 specification, fixing a bug introduced alongside a previously fixed UAC3 feature unit sub-type typo. No other files are affected.

Here is the commit message:
ALSA: usb-audio: Use correct version for UAC3 header
 validation

The entry of the validators table for UAC3 AC header descriptor is
defined with the wrong protocol version UAC_VERSION_2, while it should
have been UAC_VERSION_3.  This results in the validator never matching
for actual UAC3 devices (protocol == UAC_VERSION_3), causing their
header descriptors to bypass validation entirely.  A malicious USB
device presenting a truncated UAC3 header could exploit this to cause
out-of-bounds reads when the driver later accesses unvalidated
descriptor fields.

The bug was introduced in the same commit as the recently fixed UAC3
feature unit sub-type typo, and appears to be from the same copy-paste
error when the UAC3 section was created from the UAC2 section.

Fixes: 57f8770620e9 ("ALSA: usb-audio: More validations of descriptor units")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Jun Seo <jun.seo.93@proton.me>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260226010820.36529-1-jun.seo.93@proton.me
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>

Here is the root cause:
The bug originates from a copy-paste error when the UAC3 section of the audio descriptor validators table was created from the UAC2 section. The entry for the UAC3 AC header descriptor was mistakenly assigned the protocol version `UAC_VERSION_2` instead of the correct `UAC_VERSION_3`. This caused the validator to never match for actual UAC3 devices (which set protocol to UAC_VERSION_3), so their header descriptors bypassed validation entirely. A malicious USB device could exploit this by presenting a truncated UAC3 header, leading to out-of-bounds reads when the driver later accesses unvalidated descriptor fields.

Here is the patch:
 
 	/* UAC3 */
-	FIXED(UAC_VERSION_2, UAC_HEADER, struct uac3_ac_header_descriptor),
+	FIXED(UAC_VERSION_3, UAC_HEADER, struct uac3_ac_header_descriptor),
 	FIXED(UAC_VERSION_3, UAC_INPUT_TERMINAL,
 	      struct uac3_input_terminal_descriptor),

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
FIXED(UAC_VERSION_2, UAC_HEADER, struct uac3_ac_header_descriptor),
```
Reason:
This line mistakenly uses `UAC_VERSION_2` as the protocol version for the UAC3 AC header descriptor validator. Since actual UAC3 devices report protocol version `UAC_VERSION_3`, the validator never matches, causing the header descriptor to bypass validation entirely. A malicious USB device could exploit this by providing a truncated UAC3 header, leading to out-of-bounds reads when the driver later accesses unvalidated descriptor fields.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
FIXED(UAC_VERSION_3, UAC_HEADER, struct uac3_ac_header_descriptor),
```
Reason:
This corrected line uses the proper protocol version `UAC_VERSION_3` for the UAC3 AC header descriptor validator. Now the validator will match actual UAC3 devices (which have protocol == `UAC_VERSION_3`), ensuring their header descriptors undergo validation and preventing exploitation via truncated descriptors.
